title: First 45 Days: Practical Onboarding Sprint Guide
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, micro-sprint-focused 45-day onboarding guide for ICs and early managers joining Redwood. Intended to be handed to hiring managers and new hires at offer acceptance (lightweight) and used by People Ops and hiring managers to run a tightly scoped ramp that prioritizes product understanding, first deliverables, buddy relationships, and early quality signals.

Why 45 days?
- 45 days balances early momentum with realistic time for context-building and first meaningful work.
- We break the ramp into small, measurable micro-sprints so managers and new hires get frequent feedback and clear signals for role proficiency.

Principles (short):
- Small meaningful outcomes: every 7–15 day micro-sprint should end with an observable outcome (doc, PR, runbook, demo).
- Early ownership: first deliverables are scoped to be owned end-to-end but intentionally small.
- Buddy + cross-team touchpoints: scheduled and protected time to reduce friction.
- Data and signals: use a short rubric to record hiring/onboarding signals at each micro-sprint.
- Iterate: this doc is intentionally concise and editable per team.

High-level 45-day plan (micro-sprints):
0–7 days: Welcome & Orientation (Sprint 0)
- Outcome: 1-pager "My role & first 30-day plan" drafted by hire and synced with manager.
- Activities: account access, hardware setup, benefits/HR kickoff, security and infra walkthrough (VPC/KMS basics if relevant), team intro + product orientation session.
- Buddy: assign buddy (peer in same org) and schedule 30-minute daily check-ins for first week.
- Manager actions: set calendar with 1:1 cadence, invite to team rituals, post first micro-sprint outcome to hire's onboarding thread.
- Quick checklist (to confirm):
  - [ ] Laptop+accounts verified
  - [ ] Confluence & repo access
  - [ ] Dev environment run (hello-inference example)

8–15 days: Context & Small Deliverable (Sprint 1)
- Outcome: onboarding PR or short runbook describing a small piece of the product surface (e.g., reproduce a small bug or add unit test).
- Activities: shadowing sessions, read prioritized docs (product docs + architecture 1-pager), pair on first tiny task.
- Manager: unblock dependencies, confirm small prioritized task, join first pairing session.
- Signal to record: execution quality, communication, technical understanding.

16–30 days: Deeper Domain Work (Sprint 2)
- Outcome: deliver a scoped feature or quality-of-life improvement with a demo to the team and a brief retrospective note.
- Activities: design sync, cross-team touchpoints (infra, SRE, product), writing a short test/metric to validate change.
- Manager: arrange a canary reviewer and ensure deployment path exists.
- Signal: independent problem-solving, triage behavior, ability to ask correct clarifying questions.

31–45 days: Consolidate & Plan Forward (Sprint 3)
- Outcome: handoff-ready artifact (runbook, doc, or merged feature); a 45-day check-in with manager that sets goals for next 90 days.
- Activities: knowledge-sharing session (20–30 minutes) to the team, identify two priority growth areas, and optional shadowing for customer or support-facing teams.
- Manager: finalize performance signals and calibrate final ramp decision (green/yellow/red) using short rubric.

Compact onboarding rubric (use at day 15, 30, 45)
- Categories (score each: 1=needs-work, 2=progressing, 3=meets-expectations, 4=exceeds):
  - Role clarity and goal ownership
  - Technical/domain understanding
  - Code quality & delivery cadence
  - Cross-team communication
  - Reliability & incident awareness
- Brief notes (one-line) required per category during 30m calibration meeting.
- Outcome mapping: scores <=2 in multiple categories -> targeted 30-day support plan; 3+ across categories = standard ramp; 4s = consider stretch tasks.

Mini hiring signals checklist (for the hiring manager to preserve interview context):
- Hard technical signals observed in interview loop (one-line each): system design depth, debugging approach, testing hygiene.
- Cultural/team fit signals: collaboration examples, feedback receptivity, written communication in take-home exercises.
- Risk flags (note): unclear answers on ownership, missing remote collaboration experience, or questions about time-zone availability.
- Recommended initial role level and stretch areas (one-line).

Lightweight interview rubric template (for later hires and loop notes)
- Area: Systems & Architecture (score 1–4, evidence: one-line)
- Area: Coding & Tests (1–4, evidence)
- Area: Product sense or applied ML reasoning (1–4, evidence)
- Area: Collaboration & Communication (1–4, evidence)
- Overall hire recommendation (Hire / No-hire / Hire with Concerns) + Top 3 follow-up questions if any

Manager playbook: running this 45-day sprint
- Week-level cadence: 1:1 weekly + weekly sync with buddy for first 3 weeks. Keep 1-hour protected for pairing during sprint 1 and sprint 2.
- Weekly deliverable review: ask for a 10-minute demo or doc review. Put feedback directly into PR or doc comments (fast, actionable).
- Escalation: if deliverables slip, convert next 7-day sprint into focused remediation with 3 clear tasks and daily 20-minute check-ins.

Checklist of assets to share at offer stage (people-ops):
- Role-specific 45-day plan template
- Team org snapshot & key contributors list
- Access guide with order-of-operations for infra-sensitive roles (who to ping for VPC/KMS)
- First-week reading list (product + infra + team culture)
- Buddy intro template message (for Slack/email)

Notes to self (fragments & TODOs):
- Consider a "first-PR" badge in internal profile to gamify early wins.
- Experiment: 45-day micro-sprint cohort retrospective every month to keep playbook fresh.
- Quick survey at day 7 and day 30 (3 question NPS-style + open comment).

Example: 45-day brief for a backend infra hire (sample outcomes)
- Day 7: produce a 1-pager on startup boot path and local onboarding hurdles.
- Day 15: open PR that adds a reproducible local bug reproduction script.
- Day 30: merge a small infra config change with test coverage and updated runbook.
- Day 45: give 20-min team demo and pair on incident runbook.

Version history (small):
- 2025-02-04 Lena Park: initial draft, micro-sprint structure and rubric.
- 2025-03-10 Marco Diaz: added manager playbook, sample outcomes, and linked artifacts.

Quick links for managers (copy these into offer templates):
- Confluence onboarding template: https://confluence.redwood.company/onboarding-templates
- Example day-1 schedule (editable): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/placeholder
- JIRA new-hire epic template: HRON-1123

If you want a trimmed checklist-only version to attach to offer emails, ping me (Lena) and I’ll export a one-page checklist that teams can adopt.

-- end --
